item_title: Memory-chip stocks extended their rally into Monday's premarket, with Micron approaching $1,000 a share.
mechanism: Sustained memory-price strength is the transmission channel by which the AI buildout shows up in consumer and industrial goods costs — DRAM and HBM tightness driven by AI datacenter demand raises the bill of materials for everything from handsets to vehicles. That makes this rally a leading indicator for a specific inflation impulse working directly against the cooling narrative that just pushed September Fed-hike odds down to ~30%. The two readings in today's digest are therefore in tension rather than merely adjacent: the rate path is being priced off soft consumer data while the same AI spending that supported Japan's GDP print is tightening a goods input.

scenarios.direction: Memory contract prices keep climbing into September and hand the Fed's hike-leaning minority a concrete goods-inflation data point that cuts against the retail-sales and consumer-sentiment softness currently driving the 30% reading.
scenarios.why: Memory is an input to a wide enough range of finished goods that sustained contract-price increases pass through with a lag, arriving in CPI well after the equity market has priced them.
scenarios.precedent: The 2021 semiconductor shortage passed through into electronics and used-vehicle CPI with a two-to-three quarter lag, and did so while consumer-demand indicators were themselves softening — the same divergence being set up here.

scenarios.direction: Alternatively the rally is a positioning artifact with no pass-through, unwinding once the SanDisk investor-day enthusiasm fades, since no new catalyst appeared today.
scenarios.why: This map's own reading is explicit that Monday's move had no new driver — it is momentum on 08-13 and 08-14 news, which is the profile of a crowded trade rather than a repricing on fresh information.
scenarios.precedent: Memory equities have twice this year run on investor-day guidance and given the move back within a fortnight without any contract price following.

context_note: capital-context.yaml's fund_flows entry already flagged AI-driven inflation pressure on tech goods and electricity from EPFR's 08-11 Global Navigator commentary, but had not connected it to a specific equity move. This connects the two, and sets it against the rate-cooling reading in the same digest.

item_title: Iran claimed a Hormuz transit-route "understanding" with Oman as the 60-day US-brokered window expired; Oman has not confirmed and oil barely moved.
mechanism: Brent's failure to move on the claim is the informative part. With a Hormuz risk premium estimated around 10% already embedded in the price, a credible de-escalation signal should produce a visible pullback; a flat tape means the market is discounting the claim rather than pricing it. The discount is rationally grounded — the claim is one-sided (Oman silent), Iran conceded the map and joint statement are unfinished, and this map's own 08-16 shipping data showed transits at zero the day before the claim was made. Traders appear to be reading it the same way they read the partial shipping-map agreement reported Friday: real diplomatic movement, explicitly short of the deal that would actually reopen the strait.

scenarios.direction: Oman confirms independently within the week, and Brent gives back a meaningful part of the embedded premium in a single session because so much of it is priced.
scenarios.why: The premium is large relative to the physical supply at stake, so confirmation from the counterparty that has stayed silent is the specific missing input rather than an incremental one.
scenarios.precedent: The 08-12 US-brokered Iran-Oman announcement produced exactly this shape — a sharp move on the initial claim that partially unwound within days once the terms proved narrower than the headline, and the market has since demanded confirmation before repricing.

scenarios.direction: Oman stays silent past a few more days and the claim decays into noise, leaving the premium intact and the ledger entry unresolved into its 08-19 due date.
scenarios.why: Silence from the party whose waters and ports the arrangement depends on is itself information, and this thread has now logged several Iranian claims of progress that no counterparty corroborated.
scenarios.precedent: Iran's earlier "agreed in principle" characterisation of the Oman talks, logged on this thread, was never matched by an Omani statement and did not produce a durable repricing.

context_note: capital-context.yaml's conflict_risk_premium reading already records iran-oman-hormuz-deal-signing as pending rather than hit. This is one more data point in that same unresolved column, and it arrives one day after the transit data that made the shutdown physically measurable for the first time.

item_title: Nvidia, OpenAI and SoftBank signed the Ohio guarantee, and the signed terms correct two numbers this map was carrying.
mechanism: The signed structure makes explicit what the vendor-financing thread has only inferred: NVIDIA is now simultaneously the compute supplier, a credit backstop for the site's land/power/shell buildout, and an equity holder in the developer — three positions in one transaction, with OpenAI as the demand side. That concentration is the actual mechanism, not the headline size. What makes it hard to price is the omission: the release names capacity (4.25 IT-GW initial, option on 3.75, 8 IT-GW customer commitment) and NVIDIA's $1.5B equity cheque, but attaches NO dollar figure to the guarantee itself. A contingent liability disclosed by scope rather than amount cannot be aggregated against the rest of the ecosystem's backstops — which is precisely the gap Moody's flagged on 08-15 about off-balance-sheet AI guarantees generally.

scenarios.direction: The dollar figure surfaces in NVIDIA's next 10-Q contingent- liabilities disclosure rather than in press reporting, and it arrives materially different from the "<$120B" currently attributed to the deal — in either direction.
scenarios.why: Securities disclosure obligations bite on quantified contingent liabilities in a way that a press release does not, and the gap between a reported number and a filed one is where this map has already been corrected once this week (the $3B SB Energy figure that turned out to be $1.5B).
scenarios.precedent: NVIDIA's own 13F on 08-14 put filed numbers on SpaceX and Intel stakes that had circulated only as estimates beforehand, and the filed figures differed materially from the estimates — the same report-then-file correction pattern, three days earlier.

scenarios.direction: Alternatively the guarantee is never given a single headline number because it is structured as a series of phase-gated commitments rather than one facility, in which case the "<$120B" framing was always a category error rather than a figure to be confirmed.
scenarios.why: The release's own language — credit support to "secure initial 4.25 IT-GW, with an option to take the remaining 3.75" — reads as tranched and optional rather than as a single quantum, and an option that may never be exercised has no fixed face value.
scenarios.precedent: Vendor residual-value guarantee programs in aircraft and industrial-equipment leasing are routinely disclosed as aggregate maximum exposure across many tranches rather than as a single deal figure, precisely because per-deal quantification misrepresents optionality.

context_note: capital-context.yaml's standing picture carries the AI-financing loop as its central open risk, and the 08-15 digest led with bond traders pricing ~$70B of off-balance-sheet backstops. This is that pattern's largest single instance moving from reported to signed — while becoming, on the specific dimension of size, less legible rather than more.
